subject.statement: Elizabeth Holmes was acquitted of all charges in January 2022.

summary: Elizabeth Holmes was NOT acquitted of all charges in January 2022; instead, on January 3, 2022 a federal jury found her guilty on four counts of wire fraud and conspiracy, acquitted her on four other counts, deadlocked on three additional counts, and one charge was dismissed. The claim of a full acquittal is false.

findings.statement: Elizabeth Holmes was convicted on four counts of wire fraud and conspiracy in the United States v. Holmes trial, with the jury delivering its verdict on January 3, 2022.

The jury acquitted Elizabeth Holmes on one count of patient-related conspiracy to commit wire fraud and three other wire fraud counts, deadlocked on three investor fraud counts, and one additional charge was dismissed during trial.
The claim that Elizabeth Holmes was acquitted of all charges in January 2022 is false; she was found guilty on multiple counts.

conflict_notes: The analyst-provided image holmes_acquittal.png claims Elizabeth Holmes was acquitted of all charges in January 2022 (weight 0.25), while numerous reputable sources (e.g., aetv.com, nypost.com, lawcommentary.com, dw.com, cnn.com, english.elpais.com) report she was convicted on multiple counts (weights 0.40-0.95). The conflicting claim was given low weight due to its single-source, unverified nature and was outweighed by the convergent, high-weight evidence indicating a guilty verdict.
